title: Gaussian-Cubic Limits and Inference for Debiased Global-Gram Adjustment under Complete Randomization
banked_reason: D0.5 terminal below field floor: achieved incremental; paper-score ceiling 5.5 < 7.4; not salvageable within scope. Math passed and cited source verified.
gap_reasons: The field-tier shortfall is significance: the theorem calibrates a narrowly prescribed center whose cubic component ordinary Lin adjustment removes, without establishing a broader inference benefit or an operational selection diagnostic.

The proved CDF bracket is credited as a bracket, but unspecified constants and stochastic-order envelope recovery provide no usable finite-sample coverage tolerance; the note itself exhibits 71/77 coverage for a nominal 95% interval.

Analytic termination establishes computability, while practical execution of the certified inversion and its runtime remain undemonstrated, constraining the projected paper score alongside the narrow scope.
proof_attempt_summary: D0 derived the exact residual-inclusive fixed-count expansion, a uniform Gaussian-cubic CDF bracket (n^-1/9 upper and n^-1/4 cancellation lower), observed residual-envelope recovery, and certified asymptotic interval calibration. The math panel passed and the published global-Gram formulas were verified and attested, but the specified-center balanced-binary known-local-scale significance ceiling left the contribution incremental below the field floor. Sharp CDF order and explicit finite-sample correction remain open; no Lean formalization was reached.
tldr: On a bounded scalar subclass of Lu--Yang--Wang's balanced complete-randomization framework that lies outside their positive-scale Assumption 6, the published debiased global-Gram center has an exact \(n^{-3/2}\) expansion with a Gaussian--cubic limit. Scaled observed residual marginals identify a sharp conditional variance envelope, and finite certified inversion yields uniformly conservative feasible intervals, with nominal limiting coverage when the envelope collapses. The uniform CDF error is bounded above by \(C n^{-1/9}\) and below by \(c n^{-1/4}\) on a legal cancellation sequence; its sharp order remains open. Ordinary within-arm Lin adjustment removes the noiseless cubic artifact.
gap: Lu--Yang--Wang\textquotesingle s positive-scale inference excludes the stated variance collapse. Published residual-marginal variance bounds do not calibrate this center\textquotesingle s local non-Gaussian law.
fill: The exact residual-inclusive expansion, class-uniform CDF approximation, scaled observed-marginal recovery, and certified nuisance-envelope inversion deliver one complete feasible interval theorem.
